proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a legal all-height lower envelope, a separate finite-sample honest polynomial-band upper construction, and oracle quadratic score noncancellation; the math panel passed after primary-source citation attestation and a coverage-budget premise correction. The decision panel retained kernel-substitution, novelty-positioning and ballast findings because the sharp frontier/adaptation and actual learned-score geometry/calibration remain open; the cold tier was incremental with ceiling 4.6 below the field threshold 7.4, independently confirmed as lacking a bounded repair. Formalization never began, so this archive supplies no Lean theorem, axiom audit, or promoted substrate.
tldr: The share of a population eligible under a positive conditional-mean treatment rule is identified in a balanced randomized binary-outcome benchmark with known assignment probability. A crossing critical point makes the sign-volume derivative singular. A quadratic-oracle calculation retains the full covariance contribution of nearby detached contour pieces, while uniform retention for the learned score remains open. The note proves an explicit all-height lower envelope and constructs a separate polynomial-band interval with finite-sample 90 percent honesty; matching achievability, the sharp unknown-height frontier, and primitive learned-score calibration remain open. The proved bracket records the current rate information and transition lower bounds. Sharp rates, length-optimal tuning, transition laws, and adaptation cost remain the three residual open questions.
gap: Regular treated-share inference in Chen, Chen and Gao requires a nonzero gradient on the zero contour. Its companion upper-contour theory does not specify an honest-length frontier as an unknown saddle height approaches zero.
fill: Original-record Le Cam two-point comparisons with verified full-class alternatives control the frontier, learned signed-volume geometry controls the stochastic expansion, and a quantitative primitive approximation with public bias and computation allowances controls finite-sample coverage.
